title: Paraeus: special-mercy fiducia — before, in, and after justification
source_text: LXVI. Simile quoque apud Paraeum videre est. Fiducia, inquit, specialis misericordiae in peccatore resipiscente naturae ordine praecedit justificationem: ut videri est in Publicano, qui prius ex fide implorat misericordiam, propitius esto mihi peccatori, hoc est, confidit se accepturum veniam peccatorum: concomitatur in actu enim justificationis confidit sibi remitti peccata: tandem & sequitur; justificatus enim eadem fiducia sibi esse remissa peccata descendit in domum suam. Unde postea colligit objectum speciale fidei justificantis esse promissionem Evangelii de futuro, & praesenti, & praeterito, cuivis, mihi, tibi, illi, credenti in Filium, per Filium in sanguinem ejus remittentur, remittuntur, remissa sunt peccata. Et tandem concludit his verbis, Et sic ante justificationis actum, ante dico natura, non tempore, fides vel fiducia nostra, pro objecto habet propositionem hanc de futuro, mihi credenti remittentur peccata; in ipso actu justificationis hanc de praesenti, mihi remittuntur peccata; post actum justificationis hanc de praeterito, mihi remissa sunt peccata. In l. 1. Bel. de Justif. c. 10. Responsione ad secundam rationem.
pass_a_gloss: Something similar is also to be seen in Paraeus. Trust of special mercy, he says, in the repenting sinner precedes justification in the order of nature: as is to be seen in the Publican, who first from faith implores mercy — be merciful to me a sinner — that is, he trusts that he will receive pardon of sins: it accompanies in the act, for in the act of justification he trusts that sins are remitted to him: at length it also follows; for the justified man with the same trust that sins have been remitted to him goes down to his house. Whence afterward he gathers that the special object of justifying faith is the promise of the Gospel concerning the future, and the present, and the past — to anyone, to me, to you, to him, believing in the Son, through the Son in his blood sins will be remitted, are remitted, have been remitted. And at last he concludes with these words: And so before the act of justification — before, I say, in nature, not in time — our faith or trust has for its object this proposition concerning the future, to me believing sins will be remitted; in the very act of justification this concerning the present, to me sins are remitted; after the act of justification this concerning the past, to me sins have been remitted. In book 1 of Bellarmine on Justification, chapter 10, in the Response to the second reason.
pass_b_english: Paraeus: special-mercy fiducia in the repenting sinner precedes justification by nature-order — as in the Publican who first cries for mercy, trusting pardon will come.
It accompanies the justifying act (sins are remitted to me now) and follows it (sins have been remitted — he goes home justified).
Special object: Gospel promise in future, present, and past tenses to me/you/him believing in the Son.
Before the act (by nature, not time): will be remitted; in the act: are remitted; after: have been remitted.
